history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV row 'Shiv Mandir, Lohardaga' is a generic name; the only well-documented Shiva shrine in Lohardaga district is the ancient hilltop temple at Khakhparta (Khekparta) village, about 8 km from Lohardaga town, so this file is keyed to it with the correction flagged. The temple sits directly on the surface of the hill with no foundation, built of local boulders in Rekha Deul/Nagara style similar to Odisha temples of the period; it is a protected monument. Archaeological excavations in the early 2000s revealed eight ancient temples (~3 m high) with Shiva Lingas consecrated in seven, being renovated by the ASI. The main east-facing temple (~4 m high) has an ornate carved door jamb with Sanskrit inscriptions; the sanctum holds a Shivling, with murtis of Ganesha, Surya and Nandi in front, plus uncovered Shivlings in the complex. There is no priest and no fixed worship practice; devotees do their own pujas. It draws huge crowds during Shivratri and the Shravan month. Coordinates are approximate (map POI for Shiv Dham Mandir, Khakparta).

name: Prachin Shiv Mandir, Khakhparta
town_description: Khakhparta is a village in Lohardaga district, Jharkhand, about 8 km from Lohardaga town. It sits atop a hill amid the forested, bauxite-rich uplands of the Chotanagpur plateau, and is known for its ancient 9th-10th century Shiva temple, now an ASI-protected monument.

travel.road: Accessible by road from Lohardaga town (~8 km); the temple is reached by a flight of about a hundred steps up the hill

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shivratri and the Shravan month draw the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: No fixed hours documented; accessible during daylight (no resident priest)
